historical_record.description: Sacred Heart College, burned out of its building at Eddy and Larkin Streets in the 1906 fire, put up a temporary three-storey wood-frame school behind the church on Fell Street; after the college moved on, some time after 1914, the parish school used it.

The parish's permanent school was built, a three-storey Romanesque Revival building of stuccoed reinforced concrete designed by John J. Foley, with classrooms, an assembly hall, a library and a nurse's room; the Dominican Sisters, who had taught the parish's children since 1893, ran it.
Listed on the National Register of Historic Places as part of the Sacred Heart Parish Complex, with the church, rectory, school and convent around it.
